doc.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009

title: Grimes's first recordings and early start
summary: Rowe asks about Grimes's first dates around 1957 with Shafi Hadi (Curtis Porter), Adams and Kelly; Ali notes Grimes started early.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Henry, if my figures are right it looks like your first recording date was around 1957? Does that sound right?
Generally in there: ’58, ’57, maybe ’56 before I left Philadelphia.
Yeah that’s right I have that in here. What was — were you nervous on your first recording date? I mean I would be.
I’m trying to think of who you’re referring to was on that first date? Because I had first gigs, that I call first gigs.
Shafi Hadi, Pepper Adams, Wynton Kelly.
Who was the leader for that?
Shafi Hadi, that’s not a name I know. Shafi Hadi.
Oh Curtis Porter, that’s who that was.

See ‘cause Henry was a little more advanced than I was. Henry started playing with the big timers before I even thought about leaving out of Philadelphia. He did it really fast. Man this cat was, he was something else.
He jumped right into it, huh?
Yeah he did, man. He was playing with the big timers before I even thought about getting out of Philly.
